t.n: Arts and Crafts private press movement
t.r: England, then Germany and the United States
t.d: Revival of hand-set, hand-printed books with designed types, handmade paper and wood engravings, begun by William Morris.
t.tech: hand composition, hand-press printing, wood engraving
t.auth: press colophon, edition statement, proprietary typeface, handmade paper watermark

t.d: Hand binding in full or half leather with gold and blind tooling, from trade fine binderies to unique designer bindings.
t.tech: sewing on cords, rounding and backing, sewn headbands, gold and blind tooling
t.mat: goatskin, calf, gold leaf, marbled paper
t.auth: binder's stamp inside the front cover, quality of tooling and materials

t.r: Japan; Iran, Central Asia, Ottoman Empire, Mughal India; later Europe
t.d: Colours floated on water or a size are patterned and lifted onto paper, giving unique sheets used for endpapers, covers and edges.
t.tech: floating colours, combing and raking, laying paper on the bath
t.mat: gum tragacanth or carrageenan size, pigments, ox gall, kozo paper
t.auth: each sheet a unique monotype; pattern style and size material fit period

t.d: Decoration of handwritten books with initials, borders, miniatures and burnished gold.
t.tech: pen and brush painting, gold leaf or shell gold, burnishing
t.mat: vellum, parchment, mineral and organic pigments, gold
t.auth: parchment, pigments and script consistent with period; style (Insular, Carolingian, Ottonian, Romanesque, Gothic)

t.d: Illuminated manuscripts in leather bindings with fore-edge and envelope flaps, stored lying flat.
t.tech: blind-tooling, block-stamped medallions, gold tooling, gilt painting
t.auth: flap structure, medallion-and-pendant stamping; binding may be later than the text block

t.d: Parchment books in Ge'ez script, sewn with unsupported link-stitch and laced into wooden boards.
t.tech: link-stitch sewing, red and black ink rubrication
t.auth: palaeography of the Ge'ez hand; board and sewing structure

t.d: Traditional Japanese book forms from scrolls to pouch-bound fukuro-toji books printed from woodblocks.
t.auth: washi paper rather than wood-pulp paper; woodblock impression

t.d: Side-stitched xianzhuang binding of folded leaves with silk cord, kept in cloth cases.
t.tech: folding printed sheets, punching four or six holes, stitching with double silk cord
t.mat: xuan paper, dyed paper or silk covers, white silk cord
t.auth: hole count (Chinese even, Korean odd); paper and cover material

t.d: Texts incised into dried palm leaves and blackened, with leaves strung together through holes.
t.tech: stylus incision, colourant wiped into the grooves
t.auth: leaf preparation, script and regional format

t.d: Commercial map and atlas publishing in the Low Countries that dominated European map production.
t.auth: text language and edition on the verso, paper and platemark, contemporary versus later colour

t.d: Commercially printed woodblock maps of Japan and its provinces, from the decorative Ryūsen-zu to the more accurate Sekisui-zu.
t.tech: woodblock printing, colour printing, hand tinting
t.auth: edition and block revisions, place-name count, colouring
